questions.q: Which feature best describes the Sudan savanna vegetation zone found in northern Nigeria?
options: Mixed grasses with scattered drought-resistant trees and a distinct wet and dry season
Open desert with no vegetation except occasional succulents
Continuous dense forest with tall evergreen trees and heavy rainfall year-round
Lowland swamp vegetation dominated by mangroves and water-tolerant plants
questions.explanation: The Sudan savanna is characterised by a grassland cover interspersed with scattered, drought-resistant trees (e.g., acacia) and distinct wet and dry seasons. Dense evergreen forest and mangrove swamp describe rainforest and coastal swamp zones, while an open desert lacks the grasses and scattered trees of savanna.

questions.q: Laterite soils in parts of southwestern Nigeria are commonly used for which practical purpose because of their properties when exposed to air?
options: Road surfacing and building foundations because they harden on exposure and provide a firm layer
Making bricks that dissolve easily in rain and therefore suitable for temporary shelters
Irrigated horticulture because laterites are high in organic matter and extremely fertile
Growing rice paddies because they hold water very well
questions.explanation: Laterite becomes hard and compact when exposed, making it useful for road surfacing and foundations. It is not particularly water-retentive like paddy soils, nor high in organic matter; it is often low in fertility. Bricks that dissolve in rain would be unsuitable, so that option is incorrect.

questions.q: An ox-bow lake forms in a mature river mainly by which sequence of processes?
options: Longshore drift depositing sand to join two meander loops
Erosion on the outside of meander bends and deposition across the neck until the meander is cut off
Tectonic uplift forcing the river into a straight channel
Groundwater sapping that enlarges the channel uniformly
questions.explanation: Ox-bow lakes form when continued lateral erosion on outer bends and deposition on inner bends narrows the meander neck, which eventually gets breached and cut off. Tectonic uplift or groundwater sapping are not the usual causes, and longshore drift is a coastal process unrelated to river meanders.

questions.q: Which coastal process most directly causes the formation of a tombolo (a sand connection between an island and the mainland)?
options: Glacial deposition during the last Ice Age depositing moraine between island and shore
Tidal scouring removing all sediments to expose bedrock
Wave refraction and deposition of eroded sediments in the lee of the island forming a sand bar
Strong offshore currents eroding the island until it sinks
questions.explanation: A tombolo forms when waves refract around an island, causing deposition of sediments in the calm lee and eventually building a sand bar that connects to the mainland. Offshore currents that erode or tidal scouring that remove sediments would prevent such deposition. Glacial moraine is irrelevant in tropical Nigerian coastal settings.

questions.q: On a topographic map two points P and Q have elevations 700 m and 300 m respectively. The horizontal ground distance between them measured on the map is 4.0 km. What is the gradient from P down to Q expressed as a ratio (rise:run)?
questions.explanation: Gradient = vertical change / horizontal distance = (700−300) m / 4000 m = 400/4000 = 0.1 which equals 1:10. 1:5 would correspond to 0.2, 1:40 to 0.025, and 1:0.1 is the reciprocal (10) and therefore incorrect.

questions.q: If the time at Greenwich (0°) is 09:00 GMT, what is the local solar time at a town located at longitude 9°E? (Assume 15° of longitude = 1 hour.)
questions.explanation: Each degree of longitude equals 4 minutes of time. At 9°E the local time is 9 × 4 minutes = 36 minutes ahead of GMT, so 09:00 + 36 minutes = 09:36. 10:00 would assume a full hour ahead; 08:24 would be 36 minutes behind; 09:00 ignores longitude difference.

questions.q: How many standard time zones (each 15° of longitude) lie between longitude 15°W and longitude 30°E?
questions.explanation: The difference in longitude is 15°W to 30°E = 45°. Dividing by 15° per time zone gives 45° ÷ 15° = 3 time zones. 1 or 2 are too few and 4 would require a 60° span.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1 : 250,000 the straight-line distance between Lokoja and a neighbouring town measures 8.0 cm. What is the ground distance in kilometres?
options: 2.0 km
200 km
20 km
questions.explanation: Scale 1:250,000 means 1 cm on map = 2.5 km on ground. Therefore 8.0 cm = 8 × 2.5 km = 20 km. 2.0 km would be 0.8 cm, 200 km would be 80 cm on the map, and 0.32 km is far too small.

questions.q: A lake measures 4.0 cm² on a topographic map with scale 1 : 50,000. What is the actual area of the lake in square kilometres?
options: 0.25 km²
10.0 km²
1.0 km²
2.0 km²
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000, 1 cm on the map = 50,000 cm = 500 m on the ground. So 1 cm² on the map represents (500 m × 500 m) = 250,000 m² = 0.25 km². Therefore 4.0 cm² = 4 × 0.25 km² = 1.0 km². The other options are incorrect by simple multiplication errors.

questions.q: Which factor is most important in explaining why Lagos has become Nigeria's largest city and main port?
options: Government policy that prevented any industrial development elsewhere in Nigeria
The presence of large mineral deposits beneath the city that attracted mining industries
Its coastal site with a deep natural lagoon and good harbour combined with historical trade and investment
Its location on the continental interior far from the coast which favoured overland trade
questions.explanation: Lagos's coastal site with a deep lagoon and natural harbour, along with historical trade links and subsequent investment, explains its growth as a port city. The distractors are incorrect: Lagos is not inland, it does not owe growth to mining, and national policy alone did not prevent development elsewhere.

questions.q: A town planner wants to reduce inner-city traffic congestion in Kaduna by encouraging people to travel without private cars. Which measure would be most effective?
options: Ban wheeled street vendors from all residential areas
Improve and subsidise reliable public transport links and create pedestrianised zones
Increase the number of multi-storey car parks in the city centre
Raise parking fees only in suburban neighbourhoods
questions.explanation: Improving and subsidising public transport and pedestrian zones encourages modal shift away from private cars, directly reducing congestion. More car parks or parking fees only in suburbs may encourage car use; banning vendors won't reduce car traffic significantly.

questions.q: Which characteristic best describes a 'conurbation' in the Nigerian context?
options: A rural market centre that serves only local farming settlements
A continuous urban area formed by the merging of two or more formerly separate towns or cities
An isolated village located more than 100 km from any city
A single planned capital city built on previously undeveloped land
questions.explanation: A conurbation is a continuous urban region from merging towns or cities (e.g., Lagos metropolitan expansion). A planned capital is a new town, not a conurbation; isolated villages and small market centres are rural, not conurbations.

questions.q: Which practice would most directly reduce the risk of flooding in a built-up neighbourhood in Ibadan?
options: Create permeable surfaces and restore vegetated floodplains to increase infiltration
Build higher boundary walls around each compound
Replace trees with concrete surfaces to speed runoff into drains
Increase the number of rooftop water tanks without changing ground surfaces
questions.explanation: Permeable surfaces and restored floodplains increase infiltration and storage, reducing flood risk. Replacing trees with concrete increases runoff; rooftop tanks don't reduce surface runoff; higher walls can trap water and worsen flooding.

questions.q: Which indicator best shows that a region in northern Nigeria is undergoing desertification?
options: Expansion of permanent wetlands and rice paddies inland
An increase in coastal mangrove swamp area and fish catch
A sudden increase in annual rainfall and lush forest regrowth
Progressive loss of topsoil, reduced vegetation cover and encroaching sand dunes on formerly arable land
questions.explanation: Desertification is marked by soil degradation, vegetation loss and dune encroachment. Increased mangroves or wetlands are coastal/aquatic changes, while more rainfall and forest regrowth are opposite to desertification.

questions.q: A local government in Rivers State wants to reduce solid-waste pollution in urban rivers. Which single action is likely to be most effective?
options: Prohibit the sale of plastic bottles without providing alternatives or collection systems
Charge a flat annual waste tax without changing collection frequency
Fill in small urban streams to prevent people from dumping into them
Provide regular waste collection services and clearly marked recycling points in all neighbourhoods
questions.explanation: Regular waste collection and recycling infrastructure address the root cause by giving residents a proper disposal option. Prohibition without alternatives leads to illegal dumping; filling streams harms drainage and ecology; a tax without service doesn't reduce dumping.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: During a total lunar eclipse observed from Abuja, what is the primary cause of the Moon appearing reddish (a 'blood moon')?
options: The Earth's shadow is red because of volcanic ash which directly colours the shadow
The Moon emits red light because minerals on its surface heat up during the eclipse
Sunlight is refracted and scattered through Earth's atmosphere so that red wavelengths reach the Moon while blue is scattered away
The Sun briefly changes colour during the eclipse causing red light to be sent to the Moon
questions.explanation: The red appearance is from Earth's atmosphere refracting and scattering sunlight; red wavelengths pass through and illuminate the Moon. The Moon does not emit light itself; volcanic ash may affect colour marginally but the main mechanism is atmospheric scattering. The Sun does not change colour.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which statement correctly explains why the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn are located at about 23.5° N and 23.5° S respectively?
options: They are the latitudes where day and night are always equal throughout the year
They mark the latitudes where the Sun is directly overhead at local noon on the June and December solstices due to Earth's axial tilt of about 23.5°
They are the lines where the Earth's rotation speed reverses direction
They mark the boundaries of the Arctic and Antarctic Circles
questions.explanation: These tropics correspond to the maximum declination of the Sun (±23.5°) because Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.5°. Day and night equality occurs at the equator during equinoxes, not these tropics; Arctic/Antarctic Circles are near poles; rotation speed does not reverse.

questions.q: A village population grew from 12,000 in 2010 to 14,400 in 2020. What is the approximate annual growth rate (%) assuming exponential growth? (Use r ≈ [ln(Pt/P0)]/t × 100)
questions.explanation: Pt/P0 = 14,400/12,000 = 1.2. ln(1.2) ≈ 0.18232. Divide by t = 10 gives 0.018232; ×100 ≈ 1.823% ≈ 1.8%. The 2.0% is a close but slightly high estimate; 12.0% confuses total growth with annual rate; 0.6% is too low.

questions.q: Which one of the following best explains why port cities such as Lagos have clustered industries near the harbour?
options: To avoid paying urban taxes levied on inland factories
Because port land is cheaper than inland industrial sites
To minimise transport costs for bulky imported raw materials and exported finished goods
Because ports always provide a large supply of skilled labour
questions.explanation: Industries that depend on heavy or bulk imports/exports locate close to ports to reduce freight and handling costs. Port land is usually more expensive, not cheaper. Taxes are not the primary locating factor, and ports do not guarantee a large skilled labour pool compared with urban centres.

questions.q: A goods truck travels from Kano to Kaduna, distance 200 km, at an average speed of 50 km/h. If it stops twice for 30 minutes each, what is the total journey time?
options: 4 hours 0 minutes
5 hours 0 minutes
4 hours 30 minutes
5 hours 30 minutes
questions.explanation: Travel time without stops = 200 km ÷ 50 km/h = 4.0 hours = 4 hours. Two stops of 30 minutes = 1.0 hour. Total = 4 + 1 = 5 hours. 4 hours ignores stops; 4h30min assumes only one stop; 5h30min assumes 1.5 hours of stops.

questions.q: Which transport improvement would most reduce travel time variability on the Abuja–Kaduna corridor during the rainy season?
options: Increasing the number of roadside markets
Lowering speed limits during dry weather
Introducing more frequent informal passenger stops
Upgrading road drainage and surfacing to all-weather standards
questions.explanation: All-weather surfacing and drainage prevent road damage and flooding that cause unpredictable delays in rains. More markets and informal stops increase variability. Lowering speeds in dry weather would not address rain-season problems.

questions.q: Which atmospheric condition most directly causes the formation of dew on car windows after a cool night in Ibadan?
options: Surface temperature falling below the dew point of the adjacent air
Strong daytime solar heating
Increase in air pressure near the surface
Advection of dry air over the surface
questions.explanation: Dew forms when surfaces cool below the air's dew point, causing water vapour to condense. Rising air pressure or dry air would not produce dew; daytime heating does the opposite by evaporating moisture.

questions.q: A Stevenson screen in Jos records maximum 28.0°C and minimum 12.0°C. What is the daily temperature range and what does a large range typically indicate about local weather?
options: Range 16.0°C; indicates persistent heavy cloud cover
Range 12.0°C; indicates frequent thunderstorms
Range 40.0°C; indicates humid cloudy conditions
Range 16.0°C; indicates dry air with clear skies and strong solar heating by day
questions.explanation: Range = 28.0 − 12.0 = 16.0°C. Large diurnal ranges usually occur with clear skies and low humidity (dry air), allowing strong daytime heating and rapid nighttime cooling. Cloudy or humid conditions reduce diurnal range.

questions.q: Which sequence of air mass movement over Nigeria is most likely to bring the onset of the rainy season in southeastern Nigeria (Calabar)?
options: Cold continental polar air from the Sahara moving south
Moist maritime polar air from the North Atlantic moving east
Dry continental tropical air from central Nigeria moving to the coast
Moist maritime tropical air from the Gulf of Guinea moving inland
questions.explanation: Rainy season in southeastern Nigeria begins when warm, moist maritime tropical air from the Gulf of Guinea moves inland. Polar or continental tropical air from the Sahara is dry and suppresses rain. Maritime polar air is not the relevant tropical moisture source for Calabar.

questions.q: Which farming practice would most directly improve soil structure and reduce erosion on a steep cocoa farm in Ondo State?
options: Increasing use of broad-spectrum herbicides
Ploughing up and down the slope to expose more soil
Burning crop residues annually on the slope
Planting contour hedgerows and terracing along the slope
questions.explanation: Contour hedgerows and terraces break slope length, reduce runoff speed and protect soil. Burning residues and ploughing up/down increase erosion. Herbicides do not improve soil structure and can reduce protective vegetation cover.

questions.q: A farmer applies 60 kg of NPK (15:15:15) fertilizer per hectare to a maize field. How much actual nitrogen (N) in kg is added per hectare?
options: 15.0 kg N
3.0 kg N
60.0 kg N
9.0 kg N
questions.explanation: NPK 15:15:15 contains 15% nitrogen by weight. Nitrogen added = 60 kg × 0.15 = 9.0 kg. 15.0 kg would be 25% of 60 kg; 60 kg is total fertilizer mass not N content; 3.0 kg equals 5% of 60 kg and is incorrect.

questions.q: A geologist in Jos finds a dark fine-grained igneous rock with small vesicles and olivine crystals. Which rock is it most likely to be?
options: Granite with visible quartz and feldspar
Sandstone composed of rounded sand grains
Marble formed by metamorphism of limestone
Basalt with phenocrysts of olivine and vesicular texture
questions.explanation: Basalt is a dark, fine-grained extrusive igneous rock that can show vesicles and olivine phenocrysts. Granite is coarse-grained and light-coloured; marble is metamorphic and crystalline; sandstone is clastic with sand-sized grains—none match the description.

questions.q: Which mineral property would best help a student distinguish between gypsum and calcite in the field?
options: Gypsum scratches glass but calcite does not
Calcite is always red in colour while gypsum is white
Calcite reacts (fizzes) with dilute hydrochloric acid, gypsum does not
Gypsum is magnetic while calcite is not
questions.explanation: Calcite effervesces with dilute HCl due to reaction with carbonate; gypsum (calcium sulfate) does not fizz. Neither gypsum nor calcite is magnetic. Calcite is not always red; both can be white. Gypsum (Mohs 2) does not scratch glass (≈5.5), so the scratch claim is false.

questions.q: Which factor most strongly explains the location of the Ajaokuta Steel Complex near the River Niger in Kogi State?
options: Low labour costs from a dense local population
Proximity to major coalfields for fuel
Availability of large water supply for industrial cooling and transport
Presence of high-quality limestone deposits in immediate vicinity
questions.explanation: Large steel mills require abundant water for cooling and processing and access to river transport; Ajaokuta was sited on the Niger partly for water supply and river movement of materials. Coal is not the primary fuel for modern Nigerian steelmaking, and while limestone is needed, the immediate availability of limestone was not as decisive as water and transport. A dense local population is helpful but not the most important factor for location.

questions.q: A small cassava-processing factory in Ibadan plans to run on diesel generators. Which change would most reduce its operating cost and local pollution?
options: Switch to higher-sulphur diesel because it is cheaper
Move the factory closer to the city centre to reduce delivery distances
Install a biogas digester using cassava peelings to produce methane for engines
Increase working hours so generators run at higher load
questions.explanation: Using cassava waste to make biogas provides a renewable fuel, lowers diesel purchases and reduces emissions. Higher-sulphur diesel increases pollution even if cheaper. Moving nearer the city may reduce transport costs but won't cut fuel for generators. Running generators at higher load can be more efficient, but it still uses diesel and doesn't address pollution as directly as biogas.

questions.q: Which policy would best encourage diversification of Nigeria's economy away from crude oil dependence?
options: Fix the naira exchange rate at a high value to reduce import costs
Provide tax incentives and infrastructure support for manufacturing and agro-processing
Cut public spending on roads to reduce government debt
Increase export taxes on all manufactured goods
questions.explanation: Tax incentives and infrastructure reduce start-up costs and attract manufacturing and agro-processing, promoting diversification. Increasing export taxes discourages manufacturing exports. Overvalued exchange rates make local products less competitive abroad. Cutting road spending harms infrastructure needed for industry growth.

questions.q: Which city is best described as a port city that developed into a megacity due to trade, industry and migration from across West Africa?
options: Lagos
Enugu
Kano
Yola
questions.explanation: Lagos developed as a major port and grew into Nigeria's largest megacity through trade, industry and regional migration. Kano is an inland commercial city with historic trade but not a coastal port. Enugu grew around coal and administration, and Yola is a regional administrative centre; neither matches the coastal port-led megacity pattern.

questions.q: During the Harmattan season, which change in northern Nigerian towns like Maiduguri is commonly observed?
options: Sea breeze influence increasing temperature at night
Persistent afternoon thunderstorms
Reduced visibility due to dust haze and cooler dry mornings
Increased humidity with heavy nightly dew
questions.explanation: Harmattan brings dry northeast winds carrying dust, causing haze and cooler mornings; humidity decreases. Increased humidity and nightly dew are opposite effects. Afternoon thunderstorms are associated with the wet season. Sea breezes do not affect inland northern towns like Maiduguri.

questions.q: Which soil management practice would most directly restore fertility to a degraded savanna farm in northern Nigeria?
options: Applying only potassium-rich fertiliser annually
Planting nitrogen-fixing legumes in a crop rotation system
Burning crop residues before the rainy season
Clearing remaining shrubs to increase arable area
questions.explanation: Leguminous crops add nitrogen to the soil through fixation, improving fertility over rotations. Clearing shrubs removes vegetation cover and can worsen erosion. Applying only potassium ignores nitrogen and phosphorus needs. Burning residues destroys organic matter and reduces soil structure and nutrients.

questions.q: A farmer tests a plot and finds pH 5.0 and poor crop growth. Which amendment is best to raise pH and improve fertility?
options: Increase irrigation frequency without amendments
Add elemental sulfur to the soil
Apply more urea fertiliser only
Apply agricultural lime (calcium carbonate)
questions.explanation: Acidic soils (pH 5.0) are raised by lime (CaCO3), which neutralises acidity and improves nutrient availability. Elemental sulfur would lower pH further. Urea supplies nitrogen but does not correct acidity. More irrigation won't change soil pH and may worsen leaching.

questions.q: Which process most directly forms an ox-bow lake from a river such as the Niger in its lower course?
options: Glacial melting increasing river discharge to carve new channels
Wind deposition blocking the river mouth
Lateral erosion on river bends followed by channel cut-off during high flow
Tectonic uplift raising one bank so the river diverts
questions.explanation: Meanders enlarge by lateral erosion; during flood the neck is cut off leaving an ox-bow lake. Tectonic uplift and glacial processes are not the usual mechanisms for ox-bow formation in lowland tropical rivers. Wind deposition at a river mouth doesn't create ox-bow lakes inland.

questions.q: A hill in Ekiti shows a steep slope of 35° and is made of resistant granite with fractures. Which mass movement is most likely after heavy rain?
options: Permafrost thaw slumping
Rockfall and small-scale rockslides along fractured faces
Long-runout lahars from volcanic eruption
Solifluction over frozen soil
questions.explanation: Steep fractured granite is prone to rockfalls and rockslides when rain lubricates fractures. Permafrost and solifluction are cold-climate processes absent in Nigeria. Lahars require volcanic eruption and pyroclastic material, not applicable to Ekiti granite hills.

questions.q: A research student in Abuja (approximately 9°N, 7°E) wants to calculate local solar noon. Which action will give the most accurate local solar noon time?
options: Set noon at 12:00 standard time always, because local and clock noon coincide
Use the calendar date only, since solar noon is the same every day
Estimate by watching sunrise and set and taking the midpoint without using longitude
Use the longitude of Abuja to adjust the standard time and find when the sun crosses the local meridian
questions.explanation: Local solar noon occurs when the sun crosses the observer's meridian; this requires correcting clock time using Abuja's longitude relative to the standard meridian. Solar noon varies by date and longitude, so calendar date only or fixed 12:00 are incorrect; midpoint of sunrise and sunset can be affected by atmospheric refraction and seasonal daylight changes and is less accurate than the meridian method.

questions.q: On a topographic map with scale 1:50,000 a student measures the distance between two towns as 6.4 cm. What is the ground distance in kilometres?
options: 32 km
6.4 km
3.2 km
questions.explanation: Scale 1:50,000 means 1 cm = 50,000 cm = 500 m = 0.5 km. So 6.4 cm × 0.5 km/cm = 3.2 km. The common mistakes are to forget conversion from cm to km (giving 0.32 km), or to treat 1 cm as 1 km (giving 6.4 km), or to move decimal two places wrong (32 km).

questions.q: A contour interval on a Nigerian 1:25,000 map is 10 m. Two adjacent index contours show elevations 120 m and 180 m. How many normal contours lie between them?
options: 5 normal contours
4 normal contours
1 normal contour
6 normal contours
questions.explanation: Index contours are every fifth contour if interval is 10 m. Between 120 m and 180 m is 60 m difference, which is 60 / 10 = 6 contour intervals; that includes 5 intermediate (normal) contours between the two index lines. A common error is to count intervals instead of intermediate lines or to misapply the 'every fifth' rule.

questions.q: A student uses a map protractor and finds the bearing from Ibadan to Akure is 320°. Which compass direction best describes this bearing?
options: Northwest by north (slightly west of northwest)
West by north
Northeast
Southeast
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north; 320° is 40° west of north, i.e., north-northwest or northwest by north (slightly west of NW). Southeast (140°), northeast (45°), and west by north (281.25°) are incorrect compass interpretations.

questions.q: Which factor most likely caused the rapid growth of the satellite town of Ota near Lagos in recent decades?
options: High altitude making it a health resort
Proximity to Lagos industrial zones and cheaper land encouraging peri-urban expansion
Government policy forcing relocation from Lagos to Ota
Frequent coastal flooding in Ota increasing migration to it
questions.explanation: Ota's growth is driven by its location near Lagos industries and lower land costs that attract factories and workers. High altitude is not applicable; forced relocation policies have not been the primary cause, and coastal flooding would push people away from a low-lying area, not attract them.

questions.q: A small town in Ogun State has a central market, clustered housing, and households engaged mainly in trading and services. According to settlement hierarchy and functions, which term best fits this town?
options: Metropolis
Market town
Hamlet
Industrial estate
questions.explanation: A market town serves surrounding rural areas with trading and services and typically has clustered housing and a central market. A hamlet is much smaller with limited services; metropolis is a very large city; industrial estate refers to an area zoned for factories, not a town defined by market functions.

questions.q: During a severe rainy season in a Nigerian upland area, a river's discharge increases and causes channel scouring and bedload transport. Which short-term effect on the riverine ecosystem is most likely?
options: Immediate increase in aquatic vegetation cover
Increased stability of spawning sites for fish
Long-term accumulation of fine sediments in the channel bed
Loss of benthic organisms and reduced habitat complexity due to scouring
questions.explanation: High discharge and scouring remove benthic organisms and simplify habitats by washing away substrate. It does not stabilize spawning sites (it destroys them), nor immediately increase vegetation (plants are uprooted), and it causes erosion and coarser material movement rather than immediate fine sediment accumulation.

questions.q: A Lagos neighbourhood plans to reduce urban heat island effect. Which measure will most effectively lower daytime surface temperatures locally?
options: Increase building density without vegetation to provide shade
Replace asphalt roads with darker-coloured concrete
Increase green roofs and tree canopy cover over streets and buildings
Install more street lighting to improve night-time visibility
questions.explanation: Vegetation and green roofs increase shading and evapotranspiration, lowering surface temperatures. Darker materials raise heat absorption; higher density without green space can trap heat; street lighting affects night-time light but not daytime surface temperature.

questions.q: Jos (≈9°N, 8°E) has an average annual temperature about 6–8°C lower than nearby lowland Nigerian cities at similar latitudes such as Lafia. Which factor best explains this difference?
options: Jos lies under a different latitude band that receives less solar radiation than Lafia.
Higher altitude of Jos leading to lower temperatures (environmental lapse rate).
Jos is closer to the sea so maritime influence cools it.
Jos receives much more cloud cover year-round than Lafia, reducing incoming solar radiation.
questions.explanation: Jos is located on the Jos Plateau at roughly 1,200–1,400 m above sea level; temperature falls with height (≈6.5°C per 1,000 m), so higher altitude accounts for the 6–8°C cooler average. Maritime influence is incorrect because Jos is inland, not nearer the sea. Year-round cloud cover and a different latitude band are implausible: Jos and Lafia are at similar latitudes, and seasonal cloud differences alone would not produce the consistent temperature gap explained by elevation.

questions.q: Which soil type is most characteristic of the tropical rainforest zone of southern Nigeria and commonly develops a hard iron-rich crust when exposed?
options: Lateritic soil (laterite)
Podzol
Alluvial soil
Chernozem
questions.explanation: Lateritic soils form in hot, wet tropical climates with intense leaching; they are rich in iron and aluminium oxides and may develop a hard iron-rich crust (laterite) when exposed. Alluvial soils occur on floodplains, podzols form under coniferous cool climates, and chernozems are fertile black soils of temperate grasslands, so these are not typical of southern Nigerian rainforest.

questions.q: Which process is the main cause of rounded tors and dome-shaped inselbergs (e.g., koppies) in the crystalline basement areas of southwestern Nigeria?
options: Exfoliation and differential weathering of resistant rock
Glacial plucking and abrasion
Aeolian deflation and deposition
Karst solution of limestone
questions.explanation: In crystalline basement terrains, inselbergs and tors form where resistant rock remains after surrounding rock is removed by chemical weathering and erosion; exfoliation and differential weathering are key processes. Karst requires soluble limestone, glacial processes are not relevant in tropical Nigeria, and aeolian deflation is important in arid regions rather than crystalline bedrock hills.

questions.q: If it is 12:00 GMT at Greenwich, what is the local solar time in Sokoto (approx. 5°E longitude)? (Assume 4 minutes of time per degree of longitude.)
options: 12:20 local solar time
11:40 local solar time
12:40 local solar time
12:00 local solar time
questions.explanation: Sokoto at 5°E is east of Greenwich so local solar time is ahead by 5°×4 minutes = 20 minutes; therefore when it is 12:00 GMT the local solar time in Sokoto is 12:20. 11:40 would be 20 minutes behind (west), 12:00 ignores longitude, and 12:40 would be 10° east (40 minutes ahead).

questions.q: On a topographic map with scale 1:100,000 a student measures the straight-line distance between Ilorin and Ogbomoso as 6.5 cm on the map. What is the true ground distance?
options: 13 km
6.5 km
65 km
questions.explanation: Scale 1:100,000 means 1 cm on the map equals 100,000 cm on the ground = 1 km. Therefore 6.5 cm corresponds to 6.5 × 1 km = 6.5 km. 65 km would be 65 cm on the map, 0.65 km would be 0.65 cm, and 13 km would correspond to 13 cm on the map.
